newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European bunkers jump as barges, futures rise.
newsitem.headline: European bunkers jump as barges, futures rise.

text.p: European gas oil and fuel oil bunkers jumped on Monday after sharp initial gains in barge and futures, dealers said.
However, the higher prices merely discouraged buyers, leaving business in all ports at a standstill.
Rotterdam 380 cst was $3/$4 a tonne higher, at $116/$118 fob. Gas oil was also up sharply and little affected by a late futures selloff.
The gains reversed the losses sustained in the past month. Fuel oil bunkers have fallen over $15 a tonne from a high of $127 delivered in mid-October.
Hamburg bunkers rose, but not in line with Rotterdam. Fuel oil was up $2 to $120/$122 fob.
"The prices should have risen by more, but a few people decided to try to sell some bunkers cheaply," one trader said.
The discounting, however, failed to entice buyers.
Mediterranean bunkers were, on average, $2 firmer than on Friday. Business was slack. French suppliers were on holiday.
Fujairah bunkers leapt to year-high levels of $115/$117 delivered as fuel oil cargoes firmed and Gulf shipping fuel demand improved.
